targetAudience.primary: Engineers and governance leads responsible for long-running digital employees
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands context windows, retrieval and agent task traces.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A nominal token budget or successful task can hide what memory was retained, delivered, or costly to manage.

whyNow: A primary study of 55 archived coding-agent trajectories reports semantic differences among memory objects, unequal delivered context and management cost under equal nominal budgets, and calibration gains that do not always transfer.

externalHook.description: Two runs can fit the same token budget while delivering different usable context and paying different management cost.

coreProposition: Working-memory governance must evaluate stored state, delivered context, management work, and task/process outcome separately; nominal token budget or final success cannot substitute for layer-specific, version-bound evidence.

originalValue.description: Turns the reported measurement split into an occurrence-bound evidence model for policy admission, recovery and audit.

readerTakeaway: Keep capacity, stored state, delivered context, management work and process outcome as separate evidence surfaces; revalidate every changed memory policy against the workload boundary it will govern.

supported: The source reports 55 archived coding-agent trajectories.
The study separates stored state, delivered context, management work and task/process outcome.
Equal nominal budgets can produce unequal delivery and management cost, and some calibration gains do not transfer.
unsupported: General safety for arbitrary enterprise digital employees
Identity, authorization or exactly-once effect guarantees
uncertain: The revalidation trigger for distribution shift

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument concerns general working-memory governance.

decisionReason: The study supplies a concrete negative result and mechanism from which a bounded, independently useful governance model follows.
